input.question: How do people pirate movies that are currently in theaters?
input.ground_truth: 1. Really really good camcorders. 2. Some digital channels allow you to stream movies before they are released, just hit record button. 3. Copies of movies are sent to various critics or private screenings. Those can be stolen.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do people pirate movies that are currently in theaters?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a brand new toy that just came out, and you want to show it to your friends who don’t live near you. But the toy is only in the store for a little while before it’s sold out everywhere.

Some people who really, really want to see the toy right now might take a picture of it in the store and send that picture to their friends. Or, sometimes, someone sneaks into the store, takes the toy, and makes copies of it to give to lots of people—even though that’s not allowed and is very naughty.

For movies in theaters, it’s kind of like that. The movie is only playing in the theater right now, not on TV or at home yet. Some people use special cameras or recorders to secretly make a copy of the movie while it’s playing. Then, they share that copy online, so lots of other people can watch it on their computers or phones—even though the movie company said “No, not yet!”

But that’s not fair to the people who made the movie, because they want everyone to see it in the theater first, so they can get money to make more fun movies later. So, it’s not a good thing to do!
